comments.body:
I've done some research on using the LoC BagIt library with hard and symbolic links on disk: https://wiki.duraspace.org/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=69832398 – in short, it's easy to create a data directory with hard or soft links and then create a valid Bag.

I have revised the requirements list based on the comments and the BagIt library functionality: https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/Design+-+Transparent+Persistence#Design-TransparentPersistence-Requirements
Andrew Woods I can probably take a look at this – unless this feature is needed right away. Please let me know.
Osman Din, go for it.

Hi Andrew Woods,
I can take this on to work on during the next few weeks.
I think it will fit in well with what I'm learning here at Amherst College. Sound good?
-Bethany
That would be awesome. Former user, please keep in touch with Bethany Seeger if you need this sooner than it is happening.
Bethany Seeger: Any progress on this? Or should I jump in?

Hi Esmé Cowles – I've got some stuff checked in, but I'm not sure it's totally functional yet. You can take a look at it: https://github.com/bseeger/fcrepo-camel-toolbox/tree/fcrepo-1519/fcrepo-serialization/

I'm working on testing it now and it's still a little rough around the edges.
-Bethany

Bethany Seeger: Great – I did a little work on this and here's my branch with RDF serialization working:

https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-camel-toolbox/tree/disk-indexer/fcrepo-indexing-disk

It has a working integration test, but doesn't handle binaries at all.

I've also seen some strange issues with fcrepo-camel-toolbox: building the existing project doesn't work for me. And building my fcrepo-indexing-disk module works if I build from the top level (using "mvn clean install -pl :fcrepo-indexing-disk"), but building inside the fcrepo-indexing-disk directory fails because the features.xml file can't be found.
This looks really good. However, when deleting a resource, I am seeing errors in the karaf log and the serialization is not removed.

Hi Andrew,

My latest update to the pull request should fix this issue you were seeing.

Thanks!
It seems to delete things properly now. I've tested all the scenarios I could think of, but may have missed some (in the category of "things I don't know about fedora").

Resolved with: https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-camel-toolbox/commit/4198ccc523069e28208c479a1b64e6890c9b58d8

Follow-on documentation task: https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1856

renderedFields.description:
This task is to create a Camel component that writes repository updates to disk to satisfy the need for a human-readable backup. This should be part of the https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-camel-toolbox repository along with other Camel components.

It would be ideal if such a module were configurable to allow users to define if the RDF and/or the binary resources should be persisted to disk.

This was implemented with the fcrepo-message-consumer as documented here:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/RdfPersistenceIndexer
